clients.name: Transatlantic Telephone Company
clients.title: Transatlantic relay
clients.story: The cable under the Atlantic carries a few dozen calls at a time, and the waiting list is weeks long. The company wants a satellite to relay calls and television between the continents, and will pay for the launch.

clients.name: National Weather Bureau
clients.title: Weather picture service
clients.story: Forecasters still learn of a hurricane from the ships in its path. The Bureau wants a satellite that photographs the clouds from orbit, so a storm is seen days before it makes landfall.

clients.name: Coast and Geodetic Survey
clients.title: Measuring the Earth
clients.story: Maps on either side of an ocean disagree by hundreds of metres. The Survey wants a bright satellite to track from stations around the world, to tie the continents' maps together.

clients.name: University Physics Consortium
clients.title: Radiation belt survey
clients.story: A group of university laboratories has built counters to map the radiation belts around the Earth. They have the instruments and the money; they need a ride to orbit.

clients.name: Naval Research Office
clients.title: Navigation beacon
clients.story: A ship that hears a satellite's radio note change pitch as it passes overhead can work out where it is. The Navy wants a beacon in orbit to test the idea.

clients.name: Central Radio Propagation Laboratory
clients.title: Sounding the ionosphere
clients.story: Shortwave radio fades without warning when the ionosphere shifts. The laboratory wants a sounder above the layer, listening from the top down, to forecast the fades for airlines and ships.

clients.name: International Ice Patrol
clients.title: Icebergs from orbit
clients.story: Since the Titanic sank, ships and aircraft have patrolled the North Atlantic for icebergs every spring. The Patrol wants to try spotting the ice from orbit, over water its aircraft can't reach.

clients.name: Continental Broadcasting Company
clients.title: Live across the ocean
clients.story: News film still crosses the Atlantic by aeroplane and airs a day late. The network wants a satellite to carry a live picture between Europe and America, and will pay for the launch.

clients.name: High Altitude Observatory
clients.title: Watching the Sun's flares
clients.story: Solar flares black out radio, and the air hides their X-rays from every telescope on the ground. The Observatory wants detectors above the atmosphere to watch the outbursts as they happen.

clients.name: Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory
clients.title: Weighing the upper air
clients.story: A satellite slows as it brushes the thin upper air. The Observatory's camera stations want a bright sphere to track, so that its slow fall measures how dense the air is up there.

clients.name: Spacecraft Structures Laboratory
clients.title: Counting dust strikes
clients.story: Nobody knows how often grains of dust strike a spacecraft, or how hard. The laboratory wants panels in orbit that count every hit, so designers know how thick to build a hull.

clients.name: Air Defense Command
clients.title: A target for the radars
clients.story: Radar crews need a target whose size and path they know exactly. Air Defense Command wants a calibration sphere in orbit to check its tracking radars against, pass after pass.

clients.name: Department of Terrestrial Magnetism
clients.title: The Earth's field
clients.story: Magnetic charts drift year by year, and ships take decades to survey the oceans. The Department wants a magnetometer in orbit to measure the Earth's field all round the globe in days.

clients.name: Forest Service
clients.title: Smoke over the West
clients.story: A fire lookout sees as far as the next ridge. The Forest Service wants to learn whether a camera in orbit can spot smoke and burned land across the whole West in a single pass.

clients.name: Naval Observatory
clients.title: One clock for two continents
clients.story: Clocks on either side of the ocean disagree by thousandths of a second, too much for navigation. The Observatory wants a satellite to send one time signal to stations on both shores.

clients.name: Ministry of Communications
clients.title: Relay to the Far East
clients.story: Moscow's television reaches neither Siberia nor the Far East: the country is too wide for cables and towers. The Ministry orders a relay satellite to carry programmes across eleven time zones.

clients.name: Hydrometeorological Service
clients.title: Cloud cover for the harvest
clients.story: The harvest depends on the weather, and the forecasters have no eyes over the oceans. The Service orders a satellite to photograph the clouds from orbit.

clients.name: Academy of Sciences
clients.title: Cosmic ray instruments
clients.story: The Academy's physicists have built instruments to count cosmic rays above the atmosphere. The Presidium has approved the flight, and the agency is asked to fly it.

clients.name: Main Directorate of Geodesy
clients.title: Mapping the Union
clients.story: A country this size is mapped piece by piece, and the pieces don't quite fit. The Directorate orders a satellite to track from stations across the Union.

clients.name: Institute of Terrestrial Magnetism
clients.title: Radio to the Arctic
clients.story: Shortwave links to the Arctic stations fade for days at a time. The institute wants a sounder above the ionosphere to learn why, and to warn the radio services before the fades come.

clients.name: Arctic and Antarctic Research Institute
clients.title: Ice on the northern route
clients.story: Icebreakers on the Northern Sea Route sail on ice reports days old. The institute wants pictures of the ice from orbit, so convoys can be steered along the open leads.

clients.name: State Committee for Radio and Television
clients.title: The evening programme
clients.story: Moscow's television reaches only as far as the relay towers run. The Committee wants a satellite to carry the evening programme to Siberia and the Far East as it goes out.

clients.name: Crimean Astrophysical Observatory
clients.title: The Sun above the air
clients.story: The Sun's flares upset radio and the magnetic field, and the air hides their X-rays from the ground. The observatory wants detectors above the atmosphere to catch the flares as they happen.

clients.name: Astronomical Council
clients.title: How thin the air is
clients.story: Observing stations across the Union track satellites by eye and camera. The Council wants a bright target whose slow descent will show how thin the upper air is, and how it swells with the Sun.

clients.name: Committee on Meteorites
clients.title: Cosmic dust
clients.story: Grains of cosmic dust strike anything in orbit. The Committee on Meteorites wants counters and thin foils flown, to learn how many there are and what a hull must withstand.

clients.name: Air Defence Forces
clients.title: A sphere for the radars
clients.story: The radar stations need a target in orbit of a known size to test themselves on. The Air Defence Forces want a calibration sphere put up and left there for years.

clients.name: Ministry of Geology
clients.title: A magnetic map of the Union
clients.story: Magnetic surveys find ore, but a survey party covers a few hundred kilometres a season. The Ministry wants a magnetometer in orbit to chart the field across the whole Union.

clients.name: Aerial Forest Protection Service
clients.title: Fires in the taiga
clients.story: Fires in the taiga can burn for weeks before a patrol plane finds them. The Service wants to learn whether a camera in orbit can spot the smoke across Siberia.

clients.name: Committee of Standards
clients.title: A clean time signal
clients.story: Time signals from Moscow reach the far observatories blurred by the ionosphere. The Committee wants a satellite to send one clean signal to stations across the Union.

clients.name: Ministry of Fisheries
clients.title: Where the fish are
clients.story: The fishing fleets follow the cold currents where the fish feed. The Ministry wants the ocean's surface temperature measured from orbit, to send the trawlers where the catch is.

clients.name: Lunar Science Institute
clients.title: Photographs of the near side
clients.story: No telescope on Earth can see a boulder on the Moon, and nobody knows whether its dust would bear a lander. The Institute wants close photographs and will pay for the flight.

clients.name: Army Map Service
clients.title: A map of the Moon
clients.story: Whoever lands first will need a map. The Army Map Service orders a probe to photograph the Moon's surface for its charts.

clients.name: Observatory Consortium
clients.title: Fields around the Moon
clients.story: Does the Moon have a magnetic field? A group of observatories has built the instruments to find out, and asks the agency to carry them there.

clients.name: Radio Astronomy Laboratory
clients.title: A quiet place to listen
clients.story: The Moon's far side may be the quietest place to listen to the sky, shielded from the Earth's radio noise. The laboratory wants receivers flown out to the Moon to find out.

clients.name: Lunar Landing Studies Office
clients.title: Will the ground hold?
clients.story: Some astronomers fear the Moon's plains are deep dust that would swallow a lander. The office will pay for a probe to show what the surface will bear.

clients.name: Tracking and Data Office
clients.title: Proving the big dishes
clients.story: The new dish antennas have to be proven at the Moon's distance. The office wants a probe to follow out there, to measure how well the network can track it and talk to it.

clients.name: Academy of Sciences
clients.title: The Moon up close
clients.story: The Academy's astronomers want pictures of the Moon that no telescope can take. The Presidium orders a probe.

clients.name: Vernadsky Institute of Geochemistry
clients.title: What the Moon is made of
clients.story: The Institute's geochemists have built instruments to study the Moon's rock. They need a probe to carry them there.

clients.name: Institute of Nuclear Physics
clients.title: Radiation on the way
clients.story: Beyond the radiation belts, nobody has measured what a crew bound for the Moon would meet. The institute wants its counters flown all the way out.

clients.name: Sternberg Astronomical Institute
clients.title: Beyond the edge
clients.story: The atlases show one face of the Moon and only guesses for the rest. The institute wants a closer look at the regions round the edge, to name what it finds there.

clients.name: Institute of Applied Mathematics
clients.title: The Moon's pull
clients.story: Every path near the Moon is bent by lumps in its gravity that nobody has charted. The institute wants a probe tracked closely there, to fix the Moon's field for later flights.

clients.name: Lebedev Physical Institute
clients.title: A trace of air
clients.story: Does the Moon keep any air at all, or a haze of charged gas? The Lebedev Institute wants its instruments carried there to look for the faintest trace.

clients.name: Heat Shield Laboratory
clients.title: Samples at the edge of space
clients.story: Every capsule coming home must survive the heat of re-entry. The Laboratory wants its heat-shield samples flown fast and high, then brought back to study.

clients.name: High Altitude Research Group
clients.title: Air at the edge of space
clients.story: How thin is the air at the edge of space, and what is in it? The Group wants its samplers flown higher than any balloon can go.

clients.name: Meteoritics Institute
clients.title: Catching micrometeorites
clients.story: The Institute has built traps for the dust that falls into the upper atmosphere from space. It needs a flight high enough to open them.

clients.name: University Observatory
clients.title: Ultraviolet stars
clients.story: Stars shine in ultraviolet light that the air never lets through. A university observatory wants a small camera carried above most of the atmosphere for a few minutes of looking.

clients.name: Horizon Instrument Corporation
clients.title: Finding the horizon
clients.story: Spacecraft will steer by the Earth's horizon seen in infrared, but nobody knows how sharp that edge looks from high up. The company wants its sensor flown to the edge of space.

clients.name: School of Aviation Medicine
clients.title: The pilot's heart
clients.story: A pilot's heart and breathing through the boost, the weightless arc and the return have never been recorded in detail. The school wants its sensors on the next flight.

clients.name: Ministry of Aviation Industry
clients.title: Materials for fast aircraft
clients.story: The Ministry's design bureaus need to know how skins and joints behave at speed and height. It orders test flights carrying their samples.

clients.name: Central Aerological Observatory
clients.title: The upper atmosphere
clients.story: The Observatory's samplers have flown on balloons and sounding rockets. It orders a piloted flight to carry them higher.

clients.name: Central Aerohydrodynamic Institute
clients.title: Heat on the skin
clients.story: Above three times the speed of sound an aircraft's skin glows. The institute wants the heating measured on a real flight, to check what its wind tunnels predict.

clients.name: Air Force Research Institute
clients.title: A camera for high flight
clients.story: Cameras for high reconnaissance blur in the shaking and the heat. The institute wants its new camera flown as high and as fast as anything can go.

clients.name: Institute of Aviation Medicine
clients.title: The body at the edge
clients.story: Doctors want to know what the edge of space does to a pilot: the climb, the weightless moments and the return. The institute wants its sensors on the next flight.

clients.name: Pulkovo Observatory
clients.title: Light the air hides
clients.story: The air absorbs the stars' ultraviolet light before it reaches any telescope. Pulkovo wants a small camera carried above most of the atmosphere to catch it.

clients.name: Aerospace Medicine Institute
clients.title: How the body copes
clients.story: Doctors still argue about what weightlessness does to the heart and the inner ear. The Institute wants an astronaut in orbit, wearing its instruments.

clients.name: Geological Survey
clients.title: Photographs from orbit
clients.story: A photograph taken from orbit shows a whole mountain range at once. The Survey wants a trained eye and a good camera in orbit.

clients.name: Meteorological Satellite Laboratory
clients.title: Storms seen by eye
clients.story: A camera shows clouds, but a trained eye sees more. The laboratory wants an astronaut to describe and photograph the weather passing below, to teach its forecasters what to look for.

clients.name: University Observatory
clients.title: The night side
clients.story: From orbit the airglow, the zodiacal light and the stars look like nothing seen from the ground. An observatory wants an astronaut to watch and photograph them on the night side.

clients.name: Army Food Laboratories
clients.title: Lunch in orbit
clients.story: Can a person swallow and digest weightless? The Army's food laboratories want their tubes and bite-sized cubes tried in orbit, with notes on what works and what floats away.

clients.name: Meridian Camera Works
clients.title: Pictures for the catalogue
clients.story: A camera maker wants to show its film and lenses working in space, with a person to frame the shots. It will pay for a flight and a handful of colour pictures of the Earth.

clients.name: Institute of Biomedical Problems
clients.title: Medicine in orbit
clients.story: The Institute's doctors want a cosmonaut in orbit with their instruments, to see what weightlessness does to the body.

clients.name: Ministry of Geology
clients.title: The Union from orbit
clients.story: Photographs from orbit could show where to look for oil and ore. The Ministry orders a flight with a cosmonaut and a camera.

clients.name: Hydrometeorological Service
clients.title: Weather from above
clients.story: A cosmonaut sees the shape of a storm front as no weather map draws it. The Service wants reports and photographs of the cloud systems passing over the Union.

clients.name: Abastumani Astrophysical Observatory
clients.title: The glow of the night sky
clients.story: The upper air glows faintly at night, and from orbit the glow lies below you as a band. The observatory wants a cosmonaut to watch it and photograph it on every night pass.

clients.name: Institute of Nutrition
clients.title: Food for a long flight
clients.story: Longer flights will need real meals. The Institute of Nutrition wants its tubes and small loaves tried in orbit, and a report on appetite, taste and crumbs.

clients.name: Ministry of the Merchant Marine
clients.title: A voice for the ships
clients.story: Ships far out on the oceans lose touch with port for days. The Ministry wants to know whether a cosmonaut in orbit can reach a ship's radio and pass its messages on.

clients.name: Universities Space Research Association
clients.title: A day of experiments
clients.story: Two crew can work and watch at once. A group of universities has a list of experiments for a flight long enough to run them all.

clients.name: Air Force Research Office
clients.title: Watching from orbit
clients.story: Can a crew in orbit spot and photograph ships and airfields? The Air Force wants to know before it builds a station of its own.

clients.name: Public Health Service
clients.title: Heart and bone
clients.story: A day weightless is one thing, but longer flights may weaken the heart and bones. The Public Health Service wants two crew members measured before, during and after the flight.

clients.name: Naval Oceanographic Office
clients.title: Currents from orbit
clients.story: Ocean currents show from high up as bands of colour and calm water. The office wants a crew to photograph the Gulf Stream and the coasts, with notes on what the eye can see.

clients.name: Polaris Instrument Company
clients.title: A navigator's sextant
clients.story: Could a crew find their own position from the stars, as a ship's navigator does? An instrument maker wants its sextant tried in orbit, the sightings checked against the tracking.

clients.name: Human Factors Laboratory
clients.title: Timing the chores
clients.story: Simple tasks, turning a bolt or writing a note, take longer weightless, and nobody knows by how much. The laboratory wants a crew to time a list of chores for it.

clients.name: Academy of Sciences
clients.title: A laboratory in orbit
clients.story: The Academy wants a crew in orbit to run its experiments by hand, from growing plants to the way liquids behave.

clients.name: Ministry of Defence
clients.title: Reconnaissance from orbit
clients.story: The Ministry orders a crewed flight to test whether cosmonauts can observe and photograph from orbit.

clients.name: Military Medical Academy
clients.title: A doctor aboard
clients.story: The Academy wants one of the crew to examine the other in flight: pulse, blood pressure, reflexes and a blood sample, taken by hand in a weightless cabin.

clients.name: Institute of Oceanology
clients.title: The colour of the sea
clients.story: Plankton, silt and currents tint the sea in ways a ship can't see. The Institute of Oceanology wants a crew to photograph the oceans and describe their colours.

clients.name: Long-Range Aviation
clients.title: Steering by the stars
clients.story: Bomber navigators fix their position by the stars. Long-Range Aviation wants a crew to try the same from orbit, so a spacecraft could find its way if radio contact were lost.

clients.name: Institute of Psychology
clients.title: Two in a small cabin
clients.story: How do two people share a cramped cabin, and how well do they think in it? The institute wants tests of attention and memory run in flight.

clients.name: Orbital Laboratory Office
clients.title: Rehearsing a station
clients.story: Before anyone builds a station, someone must show that a crew can live and work in orbit for days. The Office pays for the rehearsal.

clients.name: Earth Resources Program
clients.title: Crops and coastlines
clients.story: Photographs from orbit in several colours could show diseased crops and polluted coasts. The Program wants a crew to take them.

clients.name: National Institutes of Health
clients.title: A medical log
clients.story: Three people for days in one cabin: what happens to sleep, appetite and blood? The Institutes want a full medical log of the flight, and samples to take home.

clients.name: Space Telescope Study Group
clients.title: Aiming by hand
clients.story: Astronomers dream of a telescope in orbit. A study group wants a crew to aim a small one by hand at stars and nebulae, to learn what a person adds.

clients.name: Allied Metals Corporation
clients.title: A furnace in orbit
clients.story: Weightless, molten metal neither settles nor stirs. A metals company wants a small furnace flown, to see whether the alloys made there come out purer.

clients.name: Water Pollution Control Administration
clients.title: Plumes and haze
clients.story: Smoke and silt spread farther than anyone on the ground can see. The Administration wants photographs of river plumes, spills and city haze, taken by a crew who know what to look for.

clients.name: Ministry of General Machine Building
clients.title: Practice for a station
clients.story: The Ministry plans an orbital station, and orders a crewed flight to practise the work of living aboard one.

clients.name: State Committee for Science and Technology
clients.title: Resources from orbit
clients.story: The Committee wants a crew to survey forests, fields and ice from orbit, for the planners in Moscow.

clients.name: Ministry of Health
clients.title: Days in orbit
clients.story: A longer flight raises new questions about sleep, appetite and blood. The Ministry of Health wants a full medical log of the crew, kept day by day.

clients.name: Byurakan Astrophysical Observatory
clients.title: Stars in ultraviolet
clients.story: A telescope above the air would see stars in ultraviolet light. Byurakan wants a crew to aim a small one by hand and photograph what it finds.

clients.name: Paton Electric Welding Institute
clients.title: Welding in a vacuum
clients.story: Can metal be welded in a vacuum, weightless? The Paton Institute wants its welding unit run aboard by remote control, the crew watching from the next compartment.

clients.name: Ministry of Agriculture
clients.title: The virgin lands' wheat
clients.story: Harvest forecasts from the virgin lands come late. The Ministry wants photographs of the wheat fields from orbit, to judge the crop before it is cut.
